title: Unify latency-simulation plugins and instrumentation shims for load/eval harness
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months multiple teams have added lightweight latency simulators, adapter shims, and bespoke metric tagging for different load and eval runners (microload, loadbench, synthetic-runner). This has resulted in duplicated code paths, inconsistent metric labels across runs, and fragile migrations when we upgrade core libraries (prom-client, prometheus pushgateway client, and our internal tracing shim).

Problem: When comparing historical perf regressions we frequently need to re-map metric names and reconstruct test contexts. Several small incidents (see linked postmortem) were complicated by a mismatch between the loadgen's simulated tail-latency injection and the console dashboards’ canonical latency percentiles. Maintaining separate adapters means small improvements (e.g., upstream prom-client upgrade) require repeated, error-prone patching.

Proposal summary: Implement a unified "latency-sim plugin" API and a single instrumentation shim that provides consistent metric tags and a compatibility layer for older adapters. Goals: reduce duplication, make metric schemas stable, simplify dependency upgrades, and make it straightforward to add new simulation modes (burst, correlated errors, step-changes). The new plugin manager will load adapters by name, provide a stable driver interface, and expose a single canonical metrics surface for all harnesses and runners.

Scope: refactor microload and loadbench adapters to the new plugin interface; implement compatibility wrappers for legacy runner code; consolidate metric name/tag mapping into a single module; upgrade prom-client to v15 and the tracing shim to the latest internal tracing API; add CI/regression jobs verifying metric schema and percentile alignment.

Out of scope: changes to user-facing SDKs, production runtime serving kernel code (other than small SDK call sites used by harnesses).
acceptance_criteria: 1) All load/eval runners (microload, loadbench, synthetic-runner) can be configured to use the new latency-sim plugin without code changes beyond config. 2) Dashboard metric names and tags are identical for the same simulated scenario across runners. 3) Prom-client and tracing shim upgraded with no test regressions in CI. 4) Backwards-compatible wrapper supports legacy adapter names for at least 2 release cycles. 5) Performance regression thresholds (99th percentile, p50/p95) preserved within ±3% for smoke harnesses after migration. 6) New integration test validates percentile alignment and exports canonical metric snapshot to the perf dashboard artifacts bucket.
technical_notes:
Design: plugin manager loads plugins via a simple registry (name -> class path). Each plugin must implement: start(context), inject_latency(request_metadata), teardown(). Instrumentation shim exposes: record_latency(bucket_ms, tags[]), record_sampled_trace(id, tags[]), and a canonical tag schema: {runner, scenario, model, seq_len_bin, plugin_mode}.

Compatibility: write thin wrappers for existing adapters that map their API to the new plugin interface. Implement feature flag 'enable_unified_sim' toggled per CI job.

Dependency upgrades: bump prom-client to v15 and adapt our metric creation code (prom-client API changed: Summary -> Histogram usage). Update internal tracing shim calls to use tracing-v2 forwarders. Run full regression suite after upgrades.

Performance considerations: avoid per-token allocations in the shim hot path; use pre-allocated tag maps and object pooling for simulated requests. Add microbench that asserts shim overhead < 0.5% of per-request token cost at 512 token sequence length on our smoke nodes.

Rollout strategy: (1) library + tests behind feature flag, (2) migrate one runner (microload) and run 72-hour baseline comparisons, (3) migrate loadbench and synthetic-runner, (4) flip default flag after no regressions for 7 days and merge compatibility wrappers deprecation note.
migration_plan:
Phase 0: branch and implement plugin manager + shim behind 'enable_unified_sim' flag. Phase 1: migrate microload adapter, run canary jobs against perf-prod-data with identical seed and corpus for 72 hours. Compare metric snapshots; if regression within thresholds proceed. Phase 2: migrate loadbench, run synthetic-runner. Phase 3: remove feature flag and deprecate legacy adapters after one release (documented in release notes). If any semantic metric differences are found, perform schema mapping function with a one-week freeze on GA flag. Backout plan: if any critical regressions, flip feature flag off and trigger roll-forward PRs.

Data migration: none required in storage, but dashboards must be updated to rely on canonical tags. We'll deploy a dashboard migration script to identify old metrics and create view mappings for 4 weeks post-rollout.
qa_plan: Unit tests for plugin manager and shim, integration tests in CI that run microload and loadbench with a fixed random seed and compare canonical metric JSON snapshots. Add a new nightly perf-regression pipeline job that runs a 1-hour smoke scenario and fails if p99 deviates >5% or p95 deviates >7%. Manual validation: compare trace samples in tracing UI for a subset of runs to ensure tags align. Run the existing regression harness referenced in ENG-32145 before and after change and archive artifacts to the perf artifacts bucket.
comments: 2025-02-12 Jamal Reyes: Spike complete. Prototype plugin manager + simple adapter wrapper. Observed 0.2% overhead in microbench on c5-smoke node. Added basic tests.

2025-02-15 Maya Patel: Reviewed prototype. Request: add canonical tag 'plugin_mode' and ensure it survives prom-client histogram name normalization. Also file a compatibility checklist for dash owners.
2025-02-18 PR #2380 opened for plugin manager and shim behind feature flag. CI failing on prom-client v15 API change (Summary -> Histogram). I'll follow up with a small adapter patch.

2025-02-21 QA: ran 4-hour microload canary comparing old vs unified sim behind flag. p50/p95 alignment within 2.6%. p99 showed 4.8% divergence in one seed — investigating random seed alignment and metric bucketing differences.
2025-02-25 Jamal Reyes: Fixed bucketing logic and object pooling. Re-ran canary; p99 now within 2.9%. Preparing migration plan for loadbench next week. Linking updated PR #2382.

2025-02-28 Maya Patel: Scoped estimate updated to 8 points after accounting for extra integration tests and dashboard migration script. Marking 'In Progress' and scheduling a check-in with analytics on 2025-03-03.
